newsitem.title: USA: Economist Bergsten sees weaker dlr/yen in '97.
newsitem.headline: Economist Bergsten sees weaker dlr/yen in '97.

text.p: The United States seems likely to balance the budget next year, which would inspire a bond market rally, lower U.S. interest rates and a weaker dollar against the Japanese yen, a U.S. economist said on Tuesday.

C. Fred Bergsten, director of the Institute for International Economics, said the dollar would likely strengthen against the yen over the next few months, but then weaken next year so as to end 1997 at 100 yen.

"If President Clinton does not win by too big a margin and the Republicans retain control of Congress, we're very likely to get a credible program to balance the U.S. budget over the next four or five years," Bergsten said at a forum sponsored by Commercial bank of New York.
A balanced budget would mean a big reduction in U.S. interest rates, leading to a bond rally and 10 percent decline in the real exchange rate of the dollar, he added.
"In the very short run I can imaginge the U.S. economy rising a little bit over the next few months, simply because the U.S. ecocnomy is the only strong economy in the G7 right now."
